issue_comments.author: Oscilloscope98

Hi @K-Alex13,

On Windows, to install IPEX-LLM on Intel CPUs, you could use:

```cmd
conda create -n llm python=3.11
conda activate llm

pip install --pre --upgrade ipex-llm[all]
```

On Windows, to install IPEX-LLM on Intel GPUs, you could use:

```cmd
conda create -n llm python=3.11 libuv
conda activate llm

pip install --pre --upgrade ipex-llm[xpu] --extra-index-url https://pytorch-extension.intel.com/release-whl/stable/xpu/cn/
```

Please refer to [here](https://ipex-llm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/doc/LLM/Overview/install.html) for more info regarding IPEX-LLM installation.

Please let us know for any further problems :)

issue_comments.author: LiJiaqi96
issue_comments.body:
Thanks for your timely reply. How should I changed to bf16?  Is it correct to change the following places:  
- change line 128 and 135 in `videochat2_it_mistral.py`to `torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16`  
- change line 225 in `config_7b_stage3.py` to `fp16=False`

issue_comments.author: Andy1621
issue_comments.body:
1. Change line 128 and 135 in `videochat2_it_mistral.py` to `torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16`.
2. Set `with torch.cuda.amp.autocast(enabled=config.fp16):` to `with torch.cuda.amp.autocast(enabled=config.fp16, dtype=torch.bfloat16):` in `train_pt.py` or `train_it.py`.

issue_comments.author: LiJiaqi96
issue_comments.body:
Ok many thanks, let me have a try.  
BTW, what is the use of `fp16=True` in `config_7b_stage3.py`? In my experiment mentioned above, setting `fp16=True` will result in an error and it was solved by changing it to `fp16=False`.  And what value should I set in this place?

issue_comments.author: Andy1621
issue_comments.body: `fp16=True` will use mis precision in `with torch.cuda.amp.autocast(enabled=config.fp16)`

issue_comments.author: LiJiaqi96
issue_comments.body:
Using bfloat16 solves my problem, thanks!  
Is it correct that I set the `fp16=False` when using bfloat16?

issue_comments.author: Andy1621
issue_comments.body:
It may not correct to set `fp16=False` since it will close the mix-precision training and requires more GPU memory. 

However, `bf16` and `fp32` both work for stable training. It's okay if you have enough GPU memory.

```
RuntimeError: "_amp_foreach_non_finite_check_and_unscale_cuda" not implemented for 'BFloat16'
```   

Is it the same case on your side?

[train_log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15585894/train_log.txt)
Please refer to the log. It might not be straightforward due to the use of DDP.

issue_comments.author: Andy1621
issue_comments.body: Can you try to add `model.bfloat16()` in `setup_model()` in `share_utils.py`? Please refer the code [here ](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVideo/blob/10183826112bd7edd983b68b6d7a5faa5d370709/InternVideo2/multi_modality/tasks_clip/shared_utils.py#L40-L55)since it works for me.

issue_comments.author: LiJiaqi96
issue_comments.body:
Thanks for your suggestions. I tried to solve this issue but it doesn't work.   
Finally I find the version of the `peft` and `transformers` packages was updated due to the installation of other packages. **Using the correct version of packages solved all the errors mentioned above**.  
Sorry for the efforts and the time you paid on my issue. It's so nice of you to help me a lot.  
  
BTW, I tested the memory usage with `fp16=True` or `fp16=False`, and find the GPU memory is similar. Is it better to keep fp16=True while training?

issue_comments.author: Andy1621
issue_comments.body: Thanks for your try! I think both is ok, because the model will call `with self.maybe_autocast():` in forward function for mix-precision training.

issue_comments.body: Thanks for your suggestions :)

issue_comments.author: rnwang04
issue_comments.body:
Hi @raj-ritu17 
I think these two actually are different issues from above oneapi issue.
### For the first one, hang of gemma:
If your program hang after `llm_load_tensors: CPU buffer size = xx.xx MiB`, usually set `use_mmap` to false can solve it, you can refer to this: https://github.com/intel-analytics/ipex-llm/issues/10797#issuecomment-2063709172 to see how to add `PARAMETER use_mmap false` for your model.

### For the second, -5 (PI_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES)
`-5 (PI_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES)` means you are out of your GPU memory.
You can check your GPU memory by `watch -t -n 1 "sudo xpu-smi stats -d 0 | grep \"GPU Memory Used\""` or any other monitoring tool.
I guess this is caused by you are loading several models in your VRAM at the same time.
You can check it by `./ollama list`, and if there are several models, you can remove some of them by `./ollama rm xxxx`

evidence.issue_title: Feature: Displaying agent messages in Mesop when using agent.a_run
evidence.issue_body:
`await response.process(ui)` not working

```python
import os
from collections.abc import Coroutine
from typing import Any

import anyio
from autogen import ConversableAgent
from fastagency import UI
from fastagency.runtimes.ag2 import Workflow

llm_config = {
    "config_list": [
        {
            "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
            "api_key": os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
        }
    ],
    "temperature": 0.8,
}

wf = Workflow()


async def start_conv(ui: UI) -> str:
    agent = ConversableAgent(
        name="assistant",
        llm_config=llm_config,
    )

    response = await agent.a_run(
        message="Hello, I am an assistant. How can I help you today?",
        max_turns=1,
    )

    # This works
    # await response.process()

    # This doesn't work
    await response.process(ui)

    return await response.summary


@wf.register(name="async_workflow", description="Async Workflow")  # type: ignore[misc]
def async_workflow(ui: UI, params: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    def run() -> Coroutine[Any, Any, None]:
        return start_conv(ui)
    
   # This is used until the following issue is resolved: https://github.com/ag2ai/fastagency/issues/688
    # Run the async code from the sync context
    anyio.run(run)

    return "Workflow completed successfully!"

```

```console
line 88, in process
    for event in response.events:
TypeError: 'async_generator' object is not iterable
2025-04-16 15:34:20,323 [INFO] Workflow 'async_workflow' completed with result: Unhandled exception occurred when executing the workflow: 'async_generator' object is not iterable

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2918539-e005-42da-ad8b-8df8d92b24b5)

```

#### **Issue**  
The `.ingenious` folder, which should be located at `%USERPROFILE%\.ingenious`, is assumed to exist. However, if it is missing, the application throws a `FileNotFoundError`.  

#### **Error Log**  
```
FileNotFoundError: [WinError 3] The system cannot find the path specified
  File "C:\Users\Manuel Ng\Desktop\insight-projects\ingenious-first\.venv\Lib\site-packages\ingenious\cli.py", line 247, in initialize_new_project
    shutil.copy2(template_profile_path, profile_path)
```
This occurs because the code attempts to copy a file to the `.ingenious` folder without first verifying its existence.  

#### **Proposed Solution**  
Before performing file operations, the application should:  
1. Check if the `.ingenious` folder exists.  
2. Create the folder if it does not exist.  

#### **Steps to Reproduce**  
1. Ensure `%USERPROFILE%\.ingenious` does not exist.  
2. Run the command to initialize a new project.  
3. Observe the `FileNotFoundError` in the logs.  

#### **Expected Behavior**  
The application should automatically create the `.ingenious` folder if it is missing, preventing this error.  

#### **Environment**  
- OS: Windows  
- Python Version: 3.13  
- Package Version: v0.0.10

evidence.issue_body:
When I try to import a Web Page using also a DocumentId:

If I don't use the documentId, everything works like a charm.

Unfortunately, I'm unable to recreate the error deterministically, but trying to include directly the source code in my project, I have noticed that in case of the Exception, the error is located in the [DeleteAsync method](https://github.com/kbeaugrand/SemanticKernel.Connectors.Memory.SqlServer/blob/e87b3fc373f14e47bf7775d60750804e855a9d4f/src/KernelMemory.MemoryStorage.SqlServer/SqlServerMemory.cs#L139).

### Description

Loading a [Microsoft Phi-4-mini-instruct](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct) ([4bit quantization](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Phi-4-mini-instruct)) model fails with:
`unknown pre-tokenizer type: 'gpt-4o'`
This issue was already addressed in [llama.cpp b4792](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b4792).

### Reproduction Steps

```lang=csharp
LLamaWeights.LoadFromFile(new ModelParams("Phi-4-mini-instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf"));
```

### Environment & Configuration

- Operating system: Windows 11
- .NET runtime version: 9
- LLamaSharp version: 0.21.0
- CUDA version (if you are using cuda backend): 12


### Known Workarounds

* Download newer [llama.cpp release b4792](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b4792)
* Use `NativeLibraryConfig.LLama.WithLibrary` to use the downloaded `llama.dll`

issue_comments.author: sangyuxiaowu
issue_comments.body: This is a normal occurrence as LLamaSharp relies on llama.cpp, which updates very frequently, sometimes multiple times a day. You can directly download and use the updated DLL from the llama.cpp repository.

issue_comments.author: martindevans
issue_comments.body:
LLamaSharp is not generally compatible with any version of llama.cpp except the _exact_ version it was updated to (see the table in the readme for the versions). The llama.cpp API frequently has breaking changes, so downloading DLLs from a different version will cause all kinds of issues.

There's a WIP PR (https://github.com/SciSharp/LLamaSharp/pull/1126) which will update llama.cpp to a newer version, that should include the new tokenizer type.

evidence.issue_title: The native library cannot be correctly loaded (LLamaSharp 0.21.0)
evidence.issue_body:
### Description

- LLamaSharp 0.21.0 runs smoothly in VS code both using CPU backend and CUDA backend. (downloading the NuGet packages through dotnet CLI)
- LLamaSharp 0.21.0 also works in Unity using CPU backend (downloading the NuGet packages through NuGetForUnity)
- However, LLamaSharp 0.21.0 fails to run in Unity using CUDA backend. (downloading the NuGet packages through NuGetForUnity or other suggested solutions) 

Here is the runtime error I am getting in Unity: 
`"RuntimeError: The native library cannot be correctly loaded. It could be one of the following reasons: 
1. No LLamaSharp backend was installed. Please search LLamaSharp.Backend and install one of them. 
2. You are using a device with only CPU but installed cuda backend. Please install cpu backend instead. 
3. One of the dependency of the native library is missed. Please use `ldd` on linux, `dumpbin` on windows and `otool`to check if all the dependency of the native library is satisfied. Generally you could find the libraries under your output folder.
4. Try to compile llama.cpp yourself to generate a libllama library, then use `LLama.Native.NativeLibraryConfig.WithLibrary` to specify it at the very beginning of your code. For more information about compilation, please refer to LLamaSharp repo on github.

LLama.Native.NativeApi..cctor () (at <3426e2c6b93b4d4dae67e12e3bbd97fd>:0)
Rethrow as TypeInitializationException: The type initializer for 'LLama.Native.NativeApi' threw an exception.
LLama.Abstractions.TensorSplitsCollection..ctor () (at <3426e2c6b93b4d4dae67e12e3bbd97fd>:0)
LLama.Common.ModelParams..ctor (System.String modelPath) (at <3426e2c6b93b4d4dae67e12e3bbd97fd>:0)
LlamaSharpChat.Start () (at Assets/Scripts/LlamaSharpChat.cs:18)
System.Runtime.CompilerServices.AsyncMethodBuilderCore+<>c.<ThrowAsync>b__7_0 (System.Object state) (at <834b2ded5dad441e8c7a4287897d63c7>:0)
UnityEngine.UnitySynchronizationContext+WorkRequest.Invoke () (at <b1fe495152fd4f0180f79e56e3bccacc>:0)
UnityEngine.UnitySynchronizationContext.Exec () (at <b1fe495152fd4f0180f79e56e3bccacc>:0)
UnityEngine.UnitySynchronizationContext.ExecuteTasks () (at <b1fe495152fd4f0180f79e56e3bccacc>:0)"`

Moreover, commands such as NativeLibraryConfig.Instance.WithLibrary("<Your native library path>"); lead to compile error. 

### My Workaround
I successfully ran LLamaSharp in Unity with CUDA by downgrading to LLamaSharp 0.19.0 and LLamaSharp CUDA Backend 0.19.0. Simply installing these versions via NuGetForUnity resolved the issue.

However, I am still interested in finding a fix for this issue with LLamaSharp 0.21.0 and would appreciate any insights or suggestions.

### AsyncRedisSaver aget_tuple Checkpoint ID Fix Complete ✅

I've successfully identified and fixed the bug where `AsyncRedisSaver.aget_tuple()` was returning `None` for `checkpoint_id` while the sync version worked correctly.

#### Root Cause
The issue was in `langgraph/checkpoint/redis/aio.py` at two locations:
- Line 353: Used original `checkpoint_id` (None) instead of `doc_checkpoint_id` in config construction
- Line 364: Used original `checkpoint_id` instead of `doc_checkpoint_id` in `_aload_pending_writes` call

#### Fix Applied
**Fixed both locations to use `doc_checkpoint_id` (the actual retrieved checkpoint ID from Redis) instead of `checkpoint_id` (the input parameter which may be None).**

#### Changes Made:
1. **Fixed `langgraph/checkpoint/redis/aio.py`**:
   - Line 353: Changed `"checkpoint_id": checkpoint_id` to `"checkpoint_id": doc_checkpoint_id`
   - Line 364: Changed `checkpoint_id or EMPTY_ID_SENTINEL` to `doc_checkpoint_id`

2. **Added comprehensive test coverage** in `tests/test_async_aget_tuple_checkpoint_id.py`:
   - Test that reproduces the original bug scenario
   - Test with explicit checkpoint_id (should continue working)
   - Test with non-existent thread (should return None)

The fix ensures that `AsyncRedisSaver.aget_tuple()` now behaves identically to the sync version, returning the correct checkpoint ID from the retrieved Redis document instead of None.

evidence.issue_title: Fix: a_execute_scoring() lacks rate control for local scorers
evidence.issue_body:
The a_execute_scoring() correctly uses a semaphore to limit concurrency, but sets throttle_value=0. Hence, tasks are launched in rapid succession as soon as a semaphore slot is available. When a local scorer internally invokes a rate-limited provider (e.g., OpenAI), this results in burst traffic equal to max_concurrent, potentially exceeding provider QPS limits. This could result in temporary bans , HTTP 429 errors (rate limit exceeded), or even delays.

Suggested Fix:
Set the throttle_value to 0.1 or 0.2 to ensure QPS limits are not exceeded.

issue_comments.body:
For the important_tokens which contain several actual words (like frankie_and_bennys), you can replace underscore with the space and feed them normally, Or add them as a special token. I prefer the first option because this way you can use pre-trained embedding for their subtokens. For the ones which aren't actual words (like cb17dy), you must add them as special tokens.

`from transformers import GPT2TokenizerFast tokenizer = GPT2TokenizerFast.from_pretrained("gpt2") your_string = '[PRED] name [SUB] frankie and bennys frankie_and_bennys [PRED] cb17dy' SPECIAL_TOKENS = { "bos_token": "<|endoftext|>", "eos_token": "<|endoftext|>", "pad_token": "[PAD]", "additional_special_tokens": ["[SYS]", "[USR]", "[KG]", "[SUB]", "[PRED]", "[OBJ]", "[TRIPLE]", "[SEP]", "[Q]","[DOM]", 'frankie_and_bennys', 'cb17dy'] } tokenizer.add_special_tokens(SPECIAL_TOKENS) print(tokenizer(your_string)['input_ids']) print(tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(tokenizer(your_string)['input_ids']))`

issue_comments.body:

I've sent an upstream PR to Langchain hoping to solve this using a package relying on YT inner API instead of web scraping: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchainjs/pull/7477

issue_comments.author: whoabuddy
issue_comments.body:
Do you have [bun installed](https://bun.sh/) globally? Do you see any other errors  from the script?

Originally some of the tools had dummy arguments if they didn't require any input, but the tool calling has changed quite a bit since last update, so it might be something where the smaller models aren't understanding what to input.

There is an option to add `verbose=2` to get more output from the crew that could be helpful. You can also enable langchain debug and it shows even more, see here:

https://github.com/aibtcdev/ai-agent-crew/blob/5573e0afffe7a9ebee15259b3a250eb496b49d31/prepare_for_meeting.py#L4-L10

and

https://github.com/aibtcdev/ai-agent-crew/blob/5573e0afffe7a9ebee15259b3a250eb496b49d31/prepare_for_meeting.py#L97-L107

Happy to help track down the issue I'd like this to be as simple as fork and run! :fork_and_knife: 

*edit: also [this gist](https://gist.github.com/whoabuddy/f6efa11c32d7d2ba763a2c32608c076e) has aliases for the `pipupgrade` command, which makes updating the projects dependencies much easier by using requirements.txt but grabbing the latest version.*

issue_comments.author: yanniedog
issue_comments.body:
Problem: need to ensure the "overall_goal" component of the csv/py filename does not exceed 30 characters.

The simple solution:
- just truncate the overall_goal string after the 30th character

The sophisticated solution:
- if overall_goal is >30 characters, then before saving the csv/py, make an additional query to the LLM to summarise it as follows:
"provide a concise, precise version of the string "(overall_goal)", so that it's total length is no longer than 30 characters. Your response must strictly contain only your shortened version of the string, enclosed with double quotes. Do not add anything else to your response."

issue_comments.author: botextractai
issue_comments.body:
Hi [cl2023](https://github.com/jcl2023)

I assume that you have cloned the repo with:
`git clone https://github.com/botextractai/ai-crewai-multi-agent.git`

I further assume that you have then installed all requirements with:
`pip install -r requirements.txt`
(or in a virtual environment using Anaconda, Poetry, etc.)

This should also create the bytecode files in the `__pycache__` folders. I have just tested it on Microsoft Windows, but this might be an issue in some operating systems.

I have just done that, and it worked for me. The question is what kind of error message that you got just after the text that you have quoted. The text that you have quoted is the tool description from `./tools/sec_tools.py` .

If you run the script in Visual Studio Code, then your text (the tool description) will appear in green and a possible error message in red just blow that. I need to know this exact error message.

If you got this error message

`I encountered an error while trying to use the tool. This was the error: API error: 403 - {"status":403,"error":"API token invalid. Please get a valid token from sec-api.io"}.`

then it means that you need to replace the API key in the `main.py` file with a valid key from https://sec-api.io/login .

evidence.issue_title: failed to execute ai service locally (langgarph-react-agent)
evidence.issue_body:
I cloned this repository to conduct a trial run for 'langgraph-react-agent'.

From the README, it said that we can execute the ai service without deployment (i.e., directly call LLM on watsonx.ai)
https://github.com/IBM/watsonx-developer-hub/tree/main/agents/base/langgraph-react-agent#inferencing-the-deployment

However, I got an error like below.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b2b0757-f663-43fa-b02f-83de64f2ddfd)

The error indicates an error in sending a request to LLM without sufficient information (e.g., project_id or space_id, which is a required variable for using LLM). At this point, I added a line of code to `examples/execute_ai_service_locally.py`.

```python
client = APIClient(
    credentials=Credentials(
        url=dep_config["watsonx_url"], api_key=dep_config["watsonx_apikey"]
    ),
    space_id=dep_config["space_id"], # newly added
)
``` 

Finally, it works. 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d1bc0b7-77ec-4d8b-9448-015576a54cf7)

Could you review and confirm that this approach is correct?

fix: allow `required=False` fields to be logged in Argilla (#3846)

# Description

This PR addresses an issue with the Argilla API, since it's not handling
optional values passed as e.g. `{"required": "text", "optional_value":
None}` neither when those optional fields are not provided as part of
the payload e.g. `{"required": "text"}`.

So on, in the PR the API validation when creating new records has been
fixed to check that the optional fields are neither None nor str,
instead of applying the same check as for the required fields; plus
improving the `to_server_payload` method in the `FeedbackRecord` schema
not to include the fields with value None.

Closes #3845

**Type of change**

- [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

**How Has This Been Tested**

- [x] Add unit tests for `FeedbackRecord.to_server_payload` with
`required=False` fields
- [X] Add unit tests for the validation on the API-side when creating
records via `validate_record_fields`

**Checklist**

- [ ] I added relevant documentation
- [X] follows the style guidelines of this project
- [X] I did a self-review of my code
- [ ] I made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [X] My changes generate no new warnings
- [X] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my
feature works
- [ ] I filled out [the contributor form](https://tally.so/r/n9XrxK)
(see text above)
- [X] I have added relevant notes to the CHANGELOG.md file (See
https://keepachangelog.com/)

---------

Co-authored-by: Francisco Aranda <francis@argilla.io>
Co-authored-by: Gabriel Martín Blázquez <gmartinbdev@gmail.com>

personalized interface and helps in identifying the active account.

in the crew panel. It fixes issues with adding agents to the crew.

in the crew panel.

This commit removes a duplicate Tabs.Content tag in the account page
svelte component. This was causing unnecessary nesting and potential
layout issues. The fix ensures proper rendering of the account page.
